evidence.quote: participants judged that the policy rate was likely at its peak for this tightening cycle.

Most participants noted the risks of moving too quickly to ease the stance of policy and emphasized the importance of carefully assessing incoming data in judging whether inflation is moving down sustainably to 2 percent.

many participants suggested that it would be appropriate to begin in-depth discussions of balance sheet issues at the Committee's next meeting to guide an eventual decision to slow the pace of runoff.
they viewed that there had been significant progress recently on inflation returning to the Committee's longer-run goal.
participants remarked that while the risks to achieving the Committee's employment and inflation goals were moving into better balance, they remained highly attentive to inflation risks.
recent indicators suggested that economic activity had been expanding at a solid pace.

parsed.rationale: The minutes signal the rate peak has been reached and drop the tightening bias, setting up eventual cuts and a slower runoff, which leans dovish. That lean is tempered by repeated caution against easing too quickly and continued attention to inflation risks.
